title: Go: Closures
description: Work with closures — assign functions to variables, capture variables, create function factories, and use IIFEs.

steps.title: Assign Function to Variable
steps.description: Assign a function `double := func(x int) int { return x * 2 }` to a variable and call it with `5`, printing the result.

verification.failureMessage: Assign double func to variable, call with 5, print 10.

steps.title: Closure Capturing
steps.description: Declare `count := 0`. Create a closure `increment := func() int { count++; return count }`. Call it three times and print each result.

verification.failureMessage: Capture count in a closure, call 3 times, print 1,2,3.

steps.title: Closure Factory
steps.description: Write a function `adder(x int) func(int) int` that returns a closure adding `x` to its argument. Create `add5 := adder(5)` and call it with `10`.
hints: `return func(y int) int { return x + y }`
Each call to `adder` creates a new closure.

verification.failureMessage: Create adder(5) and call it with 10, printing 15.

steps.title: Closure State
steps.description: Write a function `counter() func() int` that returns a closure. Each call increments and returns an internal counter starting at 0. Create a counter and call it 3 times.
hints: The internal state persists between calls.

verification.failureMessage: Create a counter closure and call 3 times to get 1,2,3.

steps.title: IIFE (Immediately Invoked)
steps.description: Use an IIFE (Immediately Invoked Function Expression) `func() { ... }()` to print `"executed immediately"`.
hints: Define and call the function in one step.

verification.failureMessage: Create and invoke an anonymous function that prints 'executed immediately'.
